author: Forbes
description:
As CEO of the largest, most successful drugmaker on the planet, Dave Ricks sure spends a lot of time thinking about risk.

Eli Lilly’s weight-loss and diabetes drugs have become wildly successful beyond anyone’s imagination. Its latest 12-month revenue (through June 30) surged 50% to $79.7 billion, with Zepbound (for weight loss) and Mounjaro (for diabetes) accounting for 62% of the total. In November 2025, its market cap crossed the $1 trillion mark, making it the first pharma company to do so (it’s currently hovering around $1.1 trillion).

Lilly has more weight-loss game-changers coming. A pill called Foundayo gained FDA approval in April. It plans to submit a next-gen experimental drug, retatrutide, to the FDA in the first quarter of 2027. (People are so excited about “reta,” as it’s called online, that they’re buying substances claiming to be the drug on the black market.)

author: Forbes
description:
At the Forbes 30/50 Summit, artist, curator, and cultural advisor Noor Alsuwaidi delivers an inspiring keynote about her journey from an ambitious young girl in Abu Dhabi to becoming a pioneering force in the UAE's thriving cultural landscape.

In this moving talk, Noor shares how her father’s early belief sparked her artistic passion, how overcoming grief and studying abroad shaped her confidence, and her pivotal role in building major UAE cultural institutions—from the Dubai Culture & Arts Authority to Expo 2020 and the Louvre Abu Dhabi. She also reflects on becoming the first Emirati artist featured at Christie’s auction and her decision at age 40 to choose herself and return to full-time art practice.
